stories.title: US has to 'take care' of one or two Iran targets - Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said that the United States has knocked out much of Iran's military but it still has to "take care of" one or two targets, including a suspected nuclear site known as Pickaxe Mountain. Mr Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war that the US and Israel began at the end of February were "going fine but you know they're not very reliable". He reiterated that the US was not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had decimated Iran's military and nuclear programme. "We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Mr Trump told reporters at his Florida residence. "You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. The Iranian government has denied any nuclear work is carried out there.

Customers also took to social media to complain about the problem. According to the system status page on Revolut's website, sign-in services were "partially unavailable" for a time. In a statement, Revolt said: "We experienced a short technical issue with our app this afternoon that meant some customers were unable to log in. "The issue was quickly identified and has now been fixed, and the app is working fully for those affected.

stories.title: EY Ireland's annual revenue grows by 4.4% to €880m
stories.summary: Professional services firm EY Ireland has reported continued growth for its financial year to the end of June 2026. EY Ireland reported annual revenues of €880m on the island of Ireland, an increase of 4.4% on the €843m reported in the previous year. Revenue in the Republic of Ireland reached €810m, an increase of 3.7% on last year's revenue of €781m, it added. The company's headcount across the island stood at more than 5,600 at the end of June 2026, with almost 100 different nationalities working across all areas of the business. It now has 158 Equity Partners across the island of Ireland, including 144 in the Republic of Ireland. During the year, Taoiseach Micheál Martin officially opened its new headquarters at Wilton Park in Dublin, as well as its expanded Cork offices on Lapps Quay.

stories.title: Restored nature hits record level, still off target - UN
stories.summary: Countries are restoring about 252 million hectares of nature, a record level according to a United Nations report, but this still falls short of global 2030 targets. "This report captures the largest documented restoration effort in history," said Doreen Robinson at the UN Environment Programme. The restored area is equivalent to the size of Argentina or Algeria. But the report estimates the pace of restoration efforts must "triple" to meet the 2030 target of one billion, and funding will need to increase sharply, particularly from the private sector. Nature restoration efforts recorded in 149 countries have mostly taken place on land, with 232 million hectares involved, compared with 11 million hectares of inland waters and 5.7 million hectares of marine and coastal waters. This "lags far behind ambition in both freshwater (inland water) and marine and coastal ecosystems, yet these ecosystems are degrading at the highest rates," the report warned.

stories.title: Sharks stun off-colour Munster in damp Thomond affair
stories.summary: South African franchise the Sharks made it four wins on the bounce against Munster, as they defeated Clayton McMillan's men 3-15 on a wet and windy Saturday night in Thomond Park. Tries from Gianni Lombard and Ivan van Zyl were enough for JP Pietersen’s men to pull off a rare win on Irish soil, and compound the hosts to their third defeat in the first six weeks of the regular season. Munster dominated the early exchanges but to little avail. Early Sharks ill-discipline gave the hosts a lineout deep inside the South Africans 22, but Alex Nankivell knocked the ball on with the tryline beckoning. A minute’s applause for the late, great Anthony Foley soon followed before the Sharks got their first chance to attack, eventually getting the game’s opening score. A slalom run from full-back, and player of the match, Zekhethelo Siyaya left Munster scrambling. He kicked into the backfield before a cruel bounce of the ball sat kindly for Gianni Lombard, and away from his opposite number JJ Hanrahan, to get the Durban side off the mark. On a slippery Halloween night where local fireworks surpassed the onfield act, the first half continued in a limp fashion where handling errors trickled their way into most attacking sequences. Siyaya threatened to repeat his magic for a hat trick, but the bouncing ball came back to bite.

stories.title: Untangling the Hallowe'en story - we didn't really invent it
stories.summary: Folklorist Michael Fortune takes a deep dive into the myths and legends behind Hallowe'en... I’ve been recording and sharing content about Hallowe’en from around the country and beyond for the past 20+ years and although I spent many of these years promoting the Irish connection to Hallowe’en, I now see a lot dubious claims circulating that we invented it and it was just an Irish tradition. We certainly influenced the American tradition, but we didn’t really invent it. Most of our Hallowe’en experiences are shared with our neighbours over in Scotland, the Isle of Man, Wales and parts of England, as well as our mainland European neighbours which is tied in with their St. Martin’s Eve traditions on the 11th of November or 'Old Hallowe’en’ as it was called by some. I do not have the word count to unravel the complete Hallowe’en tangle, but I will spell out the four main distinctive elements which make up the Irish Hallowe’en experience; Food/Harvest, Mumming/Disguise, The Dead/Light and Tricks/Devilment. I will share just one with you - the Mumming/Disguise element. Unlike other parts of the county and country, the Hallowe'en tradition along the north east coast of Wexford where I grew up was very strong. Many of us grew up knowing Hallowe’en as ‘All Hollow's Eve’, ‘All Holland’ or ‘Vizzarding Night’, while in other parts of north Wexford it was known as ‘Blackmen Night’ or ‘Collicking Night’. In other parts of the country they called it Púca Night, Pookie Night, Juggy Night, Snap Apple Night and over in Newfoundland, Colcannon Night.

stories.title: Blair 'so sorry' in first comments since flight incident
stories.summary: Actress Selma Blair has spoken out for the first time since being charged with assault after a mid-air incident, saying she is "so sorry". Blair pleaded not guilty to state charges over allegations she kicked a nurse and a police officer following an incident involving crew members on a flight from Los Angeles to New York. At the time, her representatives said her alleged behaviour had been brought on by a severe medical emergency. In a video posted to Instagram, Blair said: "I know I've been quiet for a couple weeks since October 11. And you deserve to hear from me directly, and I'm sorry that it's taken this long. "There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I'm listening to them." The Legally Blonde actress said that she took the matter "very seriously" and the "very simple and the truest thing I know about myself is that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone".

stories.summary: Ireland's Fittest Family returns to our screens this Sunday with more thrills, more fierce competition and an exciting brand new location thrown into the mix. He's a firm fitness fan, and does triathlons, surfing, kite surfing and has represented Ireland in University Rugby as a medical student. stories.title: Dublin Fire Brigade reports busiest Halloween in a decade
stories.summary: Dublin Fire Brigade reported the highest number of Halloween calls it has received in over a decade last night. Chief Fire Officer Greg O'Dwyer said that, as of midnight, Dublin Fire Brigade had received 558 calls. This is an increase from the 320 fire calls responded to last year. During Halloween 2024, 494 fire calls were received. Dublin Fire Brigade described that year as their busiest Halloween in a decade. Mr O'Dwyer also reported 483 Dublin ambulance calls and 338 East Region fire calls. "A very busy night in the ERCC...that's a total of over 1,350 calls processed already," he said last night, adding that a full breakdown will be available later today. Both Dublin Fire Brigade and An Garda Síochána reported no disturbance of serious concern despite the increased number of fire calls.

stories.title: Man United crisis deepens as Chelsea win with ease
stories.summary: Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. A third defeat in a row, which made it nine matches without a win in all competitions for the first time since 1988-89, brought the inevitable chants of "you’re getting sacked in the morning" from home fans, but what will hurt most for United’s beleaguered manager will be the way he was let down yet again by senior players. Lisandro Martinez, publicly outspoken earlier this month, was booked twice inside two minutes and a more needless red card it would be hard to imagine. The second yellow, for an arm raised to Wesley Fofana, also saw a penalty conceded from which Cole Palmer made it 2-0 to Chelsea, that after Morgan Rogers had scored a brilliant solo goal to show up United’s awful finishing. The irony for Carrick is that his team had dominated the first half. They were unlucky to see Matheus Cunha’s goal disallowed, the Brazilian half a yard offside, while Amad Diallo and Bruno Fernandes gave up excellent chances. Fernandes was back in the side and captain after being dropped for his outburst against Carrick following the defeat to Como on 21 October. Even that seemed little more than a footnote in a chapter that surely now must be close to its end.

stories.title: Behind the music - David Eamon
stories.summary: Wexford soul artist David Eamon has released his debut single, Beautiful Thoughts. We asked him the BIG questions . . . A student at Dublin music college BIMM, he recently played Whelan's Ones to Watch festival, and has also supported Irish acts Esmeralda Road, Child of Prague, Syano, Dog Swim and Mount Pyrus; as well as international acts Xavier Omär (US) and MT Jones (UK). I studied Law for two and a half years before I left to pursue music. Then, I worked as a singing waiter in a Teppanyaki Restaurant. Which is part of why I love cooking (signature dish is Chicken Ramen). Yearning, but make it groovy. I write most of the songs with the guitar and then my wonderful band help me bring to life what I hear playing along in my head, but they make it so much better. Like most songwriters, I try to either create, re-create or amalgamate the songs I love and want to listen to more of. And I try to make both myself; and whoever hears them feel something in the process, either with your heart, your head or your feet. Ideally, all three at the same time.

stories.title: Israel's election revealed a divided country
stories.summary: To report on last week's general election in Israel was to report on two different countries. There is the Israel seen from abroad - a country increasingly isolated over its war in Gaza and its conduct in the Occupied West Bank, the one facing accusations of genocide, sanctions and boycotts. And then there is the Israel I found on the ground - where that global isolation, and the war that caused it, barely featured in the election campaign. In some ways, it's actually not surprising. Three years later, the attacks on 7 October 2023, the deadliest day in the country's history, remain the lens through which almost everything there is seen. In a nation very much built in the shadow of the Holocaust, those attacks revived the oldest of Jewish fears - that they could never be fully safe, not even in a state of their own. Many in Ireland, where sympathy for the Palestinians runs deep, would argue that those attacks did not happen in a vacuum - but came after decades of brutal occupation, and that Israel’s response has amounted to the collective punishment of more than two million people.

stories.title: Ballydoyle's Benvenuto Cellini lands Breeders' Cup Turf
stories.summary: Ryan Moore produced a little bit of Stateside magic as he delivered Aidan O'Brien's Benvenuto Cellini with perfection to claim the Longines Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland. It may have surprised some that the Coolmore number one had elected to ride the Irish Derby hero over stablemate and Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe third Diamond Necklace, but his decision was vindicated as the son of Frankel demonstrated a blistering turn of foot when it mattered most. Ridden with patience in mid-division, Benvenuto Cellini - whose dam Newspaperofrecord herself dazzled at the Breeders' Cup in 2018 - was still on the rail with plenty in front of him turning for home. However, Moore waited for the precise moment to strike and once the gaps opened, his mount answered his urgings to power home ahead of Francis-Henri Graffard's Map Of Stars who was another to finish well from a position in rear for second. Aidan O'Brien, who was winning the Turf for a record-extending eighth time, also secured third with the aforementioned Diamond Necklace, while the victory gave Moore a record sixth success in the $5million feature. Willie Mullins's Ethical Diamond was sixth, with Irish Champion Stakes winner Hotazhell 11th for Jessica Harrington and Johanna Walsh a place further back for Joseph O'Brien.

stories.title: Clampdown on illegal parking in Dublin to be increased
stories.summary: Motorists in Dublin will see an increase in clamping, towing and fines for illegal parking from today. The change of emphasis in dealing with illegal parking will see more patrols of enforcement officers, especially in the outer suburbs of the city. The scheme will also make complaints from business owners and residents central to its response in dealing with parked vehicles causing an obstruction. What is promised to be a more robust approach to enforcement comes on foot of a new €51 million five-year contract between the City Council and parking operator, Apcoa Group. The old contract, with Q-Park-owned DSPS, which ran for 22 years, ended yesterday. The new regime to deal with illegal and anti-social parking sees the capital divided into six separate geographic zones, each with its own enforcement patrols.

stories.title: Ocon denies disagreement with Haas became physical
stories.summary: Esteban Ocon denied reports of a violent altercation with his team after the Frenchman was dropped by Haas midway through this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix. Haas made a surprise announcement on Saturday morning that Ocon had been replaced for the rest of the weekend by Ryo Hirakawa, but offered no explanation as to why. The 30-year-old took part in second practice on Friday, after Japanese driver Hirakawa had been given an opportunity in the first, but cut a frustrated figure after rowing with his race engineer during the session. Reports followed that a disagreement between Ocon and team staff had surfaced. While Ocon admits the disagreement, he rubbished suggestions that the exchange of views turned physical. "Following the recent decision from Haas F1 Team confirming that I will not be participating in this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix, I wish to formally address some media reports and speculation surrounding the situation," a statement from Ocon read. "Last night, a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved. Whilst I acknowledge that this took place, I categorically reject any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature.

stories.title: Power eyeing up Ryder Cup tilt after injury nightmare
stories.summary: Seamus Power is confident that the best is yet to come in his career after he secured his full PGA Tour card for 2027 with a runners-up finish last week at the Bermuda Championship. Power had been at risk of facing another campaign on a 'conditional card' after missing a number of cuts on the stateside tour, as well as his home event, the Irish Open, in early September. Injuries had played their part in his fall off from his best, with the 39-year-old fearful at one stage that his career might be coming to an end. But the Waterford native says that he is growing in confidence all the time and he reckons he can get back to the sort of form that saw him reach a career high of 28 in the world rankings back in 2022. "I know more about my game. Even the adversity of the last couple of years, I feel like it will stand to me again once I get going. The injury set back was something that began brewing early in 2023 when Power noticed that something was wrong with the left side of his body.

stories.title: What next for Serbia's election winners?
stories.summary: Serbia's Student List movement won an emphatic election victory last weekend on an anti-corruption platform, defeating the party of former president Aleksandar Vučić. But what comes next for the country's incoming government, which has yet to decide who will lead it? A clear majority of Serbians elected a new government in last Sunday's parliamentary election, voting for the Student List movement over the country's former president, Aleksandar Vučić, and his United Serbia coalition. Most polls had given the Student List a one or two-point lead over the ruling party. Yet, the movement won the election by more than 13 percentage points, with 53% of the popular vote. That translates to a clear majority of 140 out of 250 seats in the Serbian national assembly. Mr Vučić, who has served as either prime minister or president since 2014, and his party, won about 39% of the vote. They will hold 104 seats in opposition.

stories.title: European round-up: Parrott starts in Betis victory
stories.summary: Troy Parrott made his first La Liga start since September in Real Betis' 2-1 win at home to Malaga. A week after Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini, in relation to Parrott's game time, expressed a desire to "manage him carefully", the 24-year-old Dubliner was in from the off against the league's bottom side. First-half goals from Marc Bartra and Pablo Fornals set the Seville club on their way, with Adrián Niño replying for Malaga with just over 20 minutes to go. Free-scoring Barcelona hit Alaves for six as they bounced back from defeat against Real Madrid in a stylish 6-1 win at the Nou Camp. There were two goals apiece for Raphinha and Lamine Yamal, as well as one from Fermin Lopez and a late topper from England's Anthony Gordon coming off the bench. Mariano Diaz grabbed the late consolation for the Basque outfit. Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane could not add a team victory to personal glory as he missed a penalty before Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich were held by rivals Borussia Dortmund in a 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena.

stories.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6bn crypto theft
stories.summary: Binance said it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for. The US law enforcement agency's statement came as Binance offered reassurances it was covering the losses from the hacking attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90% of what was stolen. Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The FBI confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5bn theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. "The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026," the statement said.

stories.title: Carrick insists he will be in charge for visit of Roma
stories.summary:
Michael Carrick said he expects to still be in charge of Manchester United in Tuesday's Champions League game against Roma after their latest defeat at Chelsea. United went down 2-0 at Stamford Bridge with second-half goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, from the penalty spot, condemning Carrick's side to a third straight defeat and a fourth in their last five matches. The visitors also had Lisandro Martinez sent off for two yellow cards, while their winless run was extended to nine games in all competitions - their worst stretch since November 1988. When asked if he would still be in charge at Old Trafford for Roma's visit, Carrick replied post-match on TNT Sports: "Yes." The under-fire former Middlesbrough head coach also said he did not feel let down by Martinez, who was booked for kicking out at Rogers and then received a second yellow card for a needless arm into the face of Wesley Fofana. Carrick added: "There is a lot of emotion, we're a great football club, and we want to win football matches.
"The supporters come, make a lot of effort, pay a lot of money to watch us play. You can see from today the boys had the game in the right place and things have gone against us.

stories.title: Revenge sweet for Brighton as City undone at the Etihad
stories.summary: Brighton avenged their Carabao Cup loss to Manchester City as they held on for a narrow 1-0 win over the Premier League leaders. Yasin Ayari's early strike proved the difference as the Seagulls delivered on manager Fabian Hurzeler's stated desire for revenge after their penalty shoot-out defeat at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday. It was a second successive Premier League defeat for leaders City after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row. Champions Arsenal will now have the chance to move above City when they travel to Liverpool on Sunday. Brighton opted to stay in the Manchester area after the cup game at the same venue and will feel their decision has been vindicated. Although they had to withstand fierce late pressure to do so, by bouncing back from the cup agony and last weekend's defeat at Liverpool, Hurzeler's side are now just two points off the top.

stories.title: Shops looted as protests in Germany escalate
stories.summary: Shops were looted in Frankfurt after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets ⁠across Germany's biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs. The protests followed a wave of demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country's longtime leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting. The German protests organised by the campaign group Gen Z Regelt - "Gen Z takes charge" in German - took place in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs. In Frankfurt, Germany's financial hub, at least two stores were looted as protests turned violent, with several more damaged and police trying to get the situation under control, according to a witness. Official numbers yesterday afternoon ⁠suggested turnout was below the 182,000 participants that organisers initially expected.

stories.title: Man charged with attempted murder of doctor in Dublin
stories.summary: A 65-year-old man has been charged with the attempted murder of a doctor at a HSE facility in Dublin yesterday. Fionnbarra Ó Tuama, with an address at George's Hill Apartments on Halston St in Dublin, appeared before a sitting of Dublin District Court this morning. He was charged with the attempted murder of Dr Kevin Kilbride on 30 October at HSE Daycare Medical Clinic, 9 Ushers Island, Dublin 8. Detective Garda Mark Dennehy gave evidence of Mr Ó Tuama's arrest, charge, and caution. He said that he gave no reply when the charge was read to him. Representing the defendant, Andrea Callan said that her client would be seeking legal aid, and that an application for bail would be made at a later date.

stories.summary: An investigation is under way following the death of a man who was in garda custody in Kildare Garda Station. The man, who was in his 30s, was found unresponsive at around 9.30am. He received medical assistance from gardaí but was was subsequently pronounced dead. In a statement, Fiosrú, the Office of the Police Ombudsman, said that its investigators attended the scene and an independent investigation is ongoing. Fiosrú said its investigations relate to incidents involving contact with gardaí where a member of the public has died or been seriously injured. "A referral does not necessarily mean a garda or gardaí have been accused of wrongdoing," it said. "Instead, it means that Fiosrú should independently investigate the incident to ascertain whether or not the act or omission of a garda or gardaí may have resulted in the death of, or serious harm to, a person."

stories.title: Firearm aimed at gardaí during attempted arrest in Dublin
stories.summary: An investigation is under way after a gun was pointed at gardaí, including a trainee garda, as they tried to carry out an arrest in Dublin. A preliminary examination of a magazine recovered from the weapon indicates it was from a "realistic imitation firearm", gardaí said. Shortly before 5am this morning, gardaí on patrol in Abbey Street in the city centre saw a cyclist acting suspiciously, who then fled when they attempted to speak to him. As they attempted to stop the cyclist, one of the gardaí was assaulted and slightly injured. Gardaí say the suspect then produced a firearm and aimed it at the three gardaí, forcing them to seek cover. He then threw the weapon into the River Liffey before fleeing the scene. Searches of the area and the river are ongoing to recover the firearm.

stories.title: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine
stories.summary: Residents of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have arrived in Ukraine after being evacuated during a US-brokered ceasefire. Residents, some draped in Ukrainian flags, disembarked buses and tearfully embraced their loved-ones. In a post on the Telegram app, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked the United States and US First Lady Melania Trump for their mediation. "When the world pays attention, people are rescued. Further steps toward de-escalation and real progress toward peace are also needed," Mr Zelensky wrote. The city in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, occupied by the Russian military since 2022, had been caught in intense fighting between the two sides that had left residents unable to escape and starving. Announcing the ceasefire last week, US First Lady Melania Trump described the city as being "on the brink of disaster" and said that without her intervention, bringing aid to its beleaguered residents would have been "impossible".

stories.title: Parsons hat-trick propels Ireland to series win in SA
stories.summary: Béibhinn Parsons scored a hat-trick of tries as Ireland overcame South Africa to conclude their year on a winning note at the Athlone Sports Stadium in Cape Town. Coming off the back of their 40-27 victory last weekend, the win means that Scott Bemand's side claim a 2-0 series over South Africa in the women's team's first ever tour of the country. While Ireland ran out relatively comfortable winners in the finish, the second test looked to be in the balance for the first hour. When Vainah Ubisi ground her way over to score for the hosts on 58 minutes, Ireland trailed 17-14. However, the tourists came strong in the final quarter, with Aoife Dalton and the unstoppable Parsons scoring twice apiece to seal the victory. South Africa, currently ranked 10th in the world and whose history in the women's game is relatively limited, began brightly, going 5-0 up early on, Unam Tose touching down after just two minutes.

stories.title: Ranganathan, Croft relieved Celebrity Traitors win is out
stories.summary: Celebrity Traitors winners Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian Croft have said they are relieved they no longer have to keep their victory a secret. Mr Ranganathan, 48, and Mr Croft, 24, were crowned winners of the BBC reality show last night, securing victory for the faithfuls after banishing traitors Maya Jama and King Kenny. Mr Ranganathan invited his fellow winner onto his BBC Radio 2 show this morning to discuss the outcome of the nail-biting Celebrity Traitors finale. When asked how he feels about their victory, Mr Croft said: "I'm so happy to be here with you. It’s so nice to talk about it. "I woke up with a light sense that I don’t have to keep the secret anymore. It’s been killing me." Mr Ranganathan agreed that the pair had been "worried", while Mr Croft recalled feeling paranoid about being seen together in public.
